question: If the radius of a cylinder is halved, what happens to its volume (assuming height remains constant)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The volume of a cylinder is directly proportional to the square of its radius: V ∝ r² × h.

Since the height (h) remains constant, the volume depends only on the radius squared: V ∝ r².

If the radius is halved (1/2), the new volume becomes (1/2)² = 1/4 of the original volume.

**∴ The correct answer is one-fourth.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius is halved, so new radius (r') = r / 2.

Height remains constant, so new height (h') = h.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder = π × r² × h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Original Volume (V₁) = π × r² × h

⇒ New Volume (V₂) = π × (r')² × h'

⇒ V₂ = π × (r / 2)² × h

⇒ V₂ = π × (r² / 4) × h

⇒ V₂ = 1/4 × (π × r² × h)

⇒ V₂ = 1/4 × V₁

**∴ The correct answer is one-fourth.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height as a cylinder has exactly one-third of its volume: V = 1/3 × πr²h.

Surface Area of a Cylinder

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2πrh. Total Surface Area (TSA) = 2πr(r + h).

Volume vs. Surface Area Dimensional Changes

If all dimensions (radius and height) of a 3D shape are scaled by a factor of *k*, the surface area scales by *k²* and the overall volume scales by *k³*.
